result.summary: Adds btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target() and related constants to the libbitcoinkernel C API and C++ wrapper. This allows kernel callers to configure automatic, manual, or disabled block pruning on btck_ChainstateManagerOptions. It also validates prune target boundaries and includes unit tests for pruned chainstate manager construction.
result.problem: libbitcoinkernel provides no way to configure block pruning on ChainstateManagerOptions. Any attempt to use libbitcoinkernel with an existing pruned data directory fails during LoadChainstate() because the block manager detects prior pruning while chainstate load options default to unpruned mode, forcing an abort.
evidence: Fixes #35627 ('kernel: can't work with pruned blocksdir')
Author notes datadir loading fails with: '[error] Failed to load chain state from your data directory: You need to rebuild the database using -reindex to go back to unpruned mode.'
result.scope_notes: The diff was not provided in the prompt, but metadata shows a small addition (+65/-0) across kernel API headers, implementation, C++ wrapper, and kernel unit tests.
result.card: Libbitcoinkernel callers cannot currently configure block pruning, which causes attempts to open existing pruned data directories to fail during chainstate load. This PR exposes btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target and manual/minimum pruning constants in the C API and C++ wrapper with boundary validation. It resolves issue #35627, allowing libbitcoinkernel consumers to load and run against pruned data directories.

risk.why: A mistake in prune target validation or options setting would only affect external libbitcoinkernel consumers attempting to initialize a chainstate manager.
